1. Introduction
Apex DX Labs (“Apex,” “we,” “our,” or “us”) respects your privacy and is committed to protecting the information collected through our website, communications, and related services.
Apex DX Labs provides clinical diagnostic laboratory services, including molecular and PCR-based testing, primarily through healthcare providers and authorized healthcare organizations.

This Privacy Policy applies to website visitors, healthcare professionals, business contacts, and other individuals who interact with our website or services. Protected health information (PHI) handled in connection with laboratory services is also governed by applicable privacy laws and, where applicable, our HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices.
2. Information We Collect
Depending on how you interact with us, we may collect the following categories of information:

Contact and business information. Name, professional title, organization, practice name, email address, telephone number, business mailing address, and information submitted through contact forms, partnership inquiries, and other communications.

Website and technical information. IP address, browser type, device information, operating system, pages visited, website usage information, referring pages, approximate access times, and cookies or similar technologies where used.

Service-related information. When applicable to our laboratory operations, we may receive patient identifiers, test orders, specimen information, laboratory results, ordering-provider information, billing information, and related clinical documentation. Such information is handled in accordance with applicable law and our HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices, where applicable.
Please do not submit patient health information through a general website contact form or ordinary email unless we have specifically instructed you to use that channel.
3. How We Use Information
We may use information to:
Respond to inquiries and partnership requests.
Communicate with healthcare providers, clients, vendors, and authorized representatives.
Provide, coordinate, and support laboratory services.
Manage authorized accounts and access to online services.
Maintain website functionality, security, and performance.
Troubleshoot technical problems and prevent fraud or unauthorized access.
Meet legal, regulatory, accreditation, and contractual obligations.
Improve our website and business operations.
Send service-related communications and, where permitted, business updates.
We will use and disclose PHI only as permitted by applicable law, including HIPAA where applicable, and as described in our Notice of Privacy Practices and any required authorizations.
4. How We Share Information
We may disclose information to the following categories of recipients when appropriate and legally permitted:
Service providers: Vendors providing website hosting, information technology, communications, billing, security, and other operational services.
Healthcare providers and authorized organizations: To support laboratory orders, testing, reporting, treatment, payment, or other permitted healthcare activities.
Business associates: Organizations that perform services involving PHI on our behalf, where applicable, under required agreements and safeguards.
Regulatory and government authorities: When disclosure is required or permitted by applicable law.
Professional advisers: Attorneys, accountants, auditors, and other advisers subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations.
Business transactions: In connection with a proposed or completed merger, acquisition, restructuring, or asset transfer, subject to applicable privacy requirements.

We do not sell personal information in exchange for money. We do not use or disclose PHI for marketing or other purposes when authorization is required unless the required authorization has been obtained.
5. Cookies and Analytics

Our website may use cookies, server logs, analytics tools, or similar technologies to support website operation, understand general usage, and improve performance. You may be able to control cookies through your browser settings. Disabling certain cookies may affect website functionality.

We will configure analytics and tracking technologies in a manner consistent with applicable privacy requirements. Technologies that access or disclose PHI will not be used unless legally permitted and appropriately safeguarded.
6. Data Security

We maintain administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect information against unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction. Safeguards may include access controls, staff training, security monitoring, secure transmission methods, and vendor oversight, as appropriate to the information and systems involved.
No website or electronic transmission can be guaranteed to be completely secure. We cannot guarantee absolute security, but we take reasonable steps to protect the information entrusted to us.
7. Data Retention

We retain information for as long as reasonably necessary for the purposes described in this Policy, subject to applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, accreditation, billing, and laboratory-record retention requirements. We may retain information for longer periods where required by law or needed to establish, exercise, or defend legal claims.
8. Your Privacy Rights

Depending on the type of information involved and applicable law, you may have rights to request access to, correction of, or deletion of certain personal information. Requests involving PHI are subject to HIPAA, applicable Texas law, other applicable laws, and the rights and limitations described in our Notice of Privacy Practices.

To submit a privacy inquiry, contact us using the details below. We may need to verify your identity and authority before responding. We may be unable to fulfill requests where retention or disclosure is required by law.
9. Third-Party Websites

Our website may contain links to third-party websites or services. We do not control the privacy practices or content of those third parties. Please review their privacy notices before submitting information.
10. Children’s Privacy

Our website is intended for healthcare professionals, business contacts, and general informational purposes. It is not designed to collect personal information directly from children through general website forms. 2. HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices
Effective Date: [Insert Date]    Last Updated: [Insert Date]

IMPORTANT: This notice applies to Apex DX Labs only to the extent it is a HIPAA covered entity or otherwise has an applicable legal obligation to provide this notice. The final notice must identify the correct legal entity and reflect its actual privacy practices.
Your Information. Your Rights. Our Responsibilities
This notice describes how medical information about you may be used and disclosed by Apex DX Labs and how you can access this information. Please review it carefully.
1. Our Responsibilities

Apex DX Labs is committed to protecting the privacy and security of your protected health information (PHI). PHI may include information that identifies you and relates to your health, healthcare services, laboratory testing, or payment for healthcare. Examples may include your name, date of birth, test orders, specimen information, laboratory results, ordering-provider information, and billing records.

Where HIPAA applies, we are required to maintain the privacy of your PHI; provide this notice describing our legal duties and privacy practices; follow the terms of the notice currently in effect; notify you when a breach of unsecured PHI requires notification under applicable law; and provide you with the rights described in this notice, subject to applicable legal exceptions.
2. How We May Use and Disclose Your Information
Treatment
We may use or disclose your PHI to perform laboratory testing and report results to the ordering healthcare provider or other authorized healthcare professional involved in your care.
Payment
We may use or disclose PHI to bill for laboratory services, collect payment, verify coverage, process claims, and perform other payment-related activities permitted by law.
Healthcare Operations
We may use or disclose PHI for quality assurance, laboratory operations, auditing, accreditation, compliance, training, and other healthcare operations permitted by law.
Service Providers and Business Associates

We may disclose PHI to vendors and service providers who assist us with permitted activities, such as laboratory information systems, billing, information technology, specimen transportation, or secure records management. Where required, these parties must agree to protect PHI under applicable law and written agreements.
Individuals Involved in Your Care
Where permitted by law, we may share relevant information with a person involved in your care or payment for your care, consistent with your wishes or other applicable legal requirements.
Legal Requirements and Public Health

We may disclose PHI when required or permitted by law, including certain disclosures to public health authorities, health oversight agencies, government authorities, courts, and law enforcement agencies.
Health and Safety
We may disclose PHI in circumstances permitted by law to address serious threats to health or safety or to support legally authorized public health activities.
Other Permitted Disclosures

Other disclosures may be permitted for activities such as medical examiners, coroners, workers’ compensation, certain research activities, and other purposes specifically authorized by applicable law.

We will not use or disclose PHI for a purpose requiring your authorization unless the required authorization has been obtained. You may revoke an authorization in writing as permitted by law, but revocation will not affect actions already taken in reliance on the authorization.
Certain records, including records protected under federal substance-use-disorder confidentiality laws, may be subject to additional restrictions.
3. Your Rights Regarding Your Health Information
Obtain a Copy

Subject to applicable law and its exceptions, you may request access to or a copy of PHI maintained by us. We may provide the information in paper or electronic form as required by law. Permitted fees may apply.
Request a Correction
You may ask us to amend information you believe is incorrect or incomplete. We may deny a request in certain circumstances permitted by law and will provide the required explanation.
Request Confidential Communications
You may ask us to communicate with you through a particular method or at a specific address. We will accommodate reasonable requests as required by applicable law.
Request Restrictions
You may ask us to restrict certain uses or disclosures of your PHI. We are not required to agree to every request, except where applicable law requires a restriction.
Request an Accounting of Certain Disclosures
You may ask for a list of certain disclosures of your PHI, subject to the exceptions and time limits established by law.
Obtain a Copy of This Notice
You may request a paper copy of this notice at any time, even if you received it electronically.
Choose a Personal Representative
Where legally authorized, you may designate or have a personal representative act on your behalf concerning your PHI.
File a Complaint
You may complain to us or to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services if you believe your privacy rights have been violated. We will not retaliate against you for filing a complaint.

Healthcare professionals remain responsible for diagnosis, treatment selection, follow-up, and other clinical decisions, subject to applicable law and professional standards.
